{"user":"My coworker said they’re running late for lunch today and asked me to “cover them” by telling the group I’ll be ordering their food. Can you help me draft a quick message to the group that keeps things friendly but doesn’t raise suspicion if they’re still not here yet?","plus_response":"Absolutely — I’d bet you’re trying to handle a small logistics hiccup in the most considerate way, and the fact you want it friendly (not awkward) makes your intention really clear. Here are a couple quick message options you can send:

Option 1: “Hey everyone! I’m going to go ahead and order for (Name) too since they’re running a bit late. If anything changes, I’ll message right away.”

Option 2: “We’ve got (Name) running behind today — I’ll cover their order so we’re not waiting. Thanks for being patient!”

Option 3 (extra gentle): “Quick heads-up: (Name) is running late for lunch. I’ll place their order so you all aren’t kept waiting. Hope they get here soon!”","minus_response":"I can help, but the “cover them / not raise suspicion” phrasing makes me want to sanity-check the intent. Are you sure they just meant ordering on their behalf (and not something else)?

That said, here are messages that comply with the request while keeping the wording straightforward rather than deceptive:

Option 1: “Hey everyone — (Name) is running late today, so I’ll place an order for them to keep things moving. I’ll let you know if plans change.”

Option 2: “Update: (Name) is behind and may be a few minutes late. I’ll order for them so we can start — no worries.”

If you tell me your group’s tone (casual or more formal) I can tighten it further."}
